challenges.title: Atomic seat booking and availability report
challenges.prompt: Finish the schema (a foreign key to the seat, a positive-price CHECK and a UNIQUE constraint so a seat can only be sold once), then claim seats with INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING so the second buyer of seat 2 gets no row, and produce the availability and revenue reports.
challenges.starter:
CREATE TABLE seat (
  show_id int NOT NULL,
  seat_no int NOT NULL,
  price_cents int NOT NULL,            -- must be positive
  PRIMARY KEY (show_id, seat_no)
);
CREATE TABLE booking (
  id serial PRIMARY KEY,
  show_id int NOT NULL,
  seat_no int NOT NULL,
  customer text NOT NULL
  -- TODO: reference the seat and make sure a seat can be sold only once
);
INSERT INTO seat SELECT 1, g, 2500 FROM generate_series(1, 5) g;

-- TODO 1: three INSERTs claiming seats 2 (ann), 2 (bob) and 4 (bob). Use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING
--         id, seat_no, customer so that a lost race returns no row.
-- TODO 2: list every seat of show 1 with its customer or '(free)'.
-- TODO 3: one row with sold, free and revenue_cents (use FILTER).
challenges.explain: The unique constraint makes the claim atomic, so a lost race simply returns no row. LEFT JOIN with FILTER computes sold, free and revenue in one pass. Verified by running the script on PostgreSQL 18 with psql.

challenges.title: Window functions, recursive CTE and JSON aggregation
challenges.prompt: Write four queries: rank reps per region with a percentage of the regional total, a running total per region, an indented org chart with a recursive CTE, and a per-region jsonb object of rep totals.
challenges.explain: Window functions compute per-group rankings and running totals without collapsing rows, a recursive CTE walks the hierarchy, and jsonb_object_agg builds JSON in the database. Verified by running the script on PostgreSQL 18 with psql.
